Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content: "469 :     public static final CSVFormat RFC4180 = DEFAULT.withIgnoreEmptyLines(false);"

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- The failing test constructs a CSVPrinter with CSVFormat.RFC4180 and prints a record whose first field is the Euro character, then asserts that the output should not quote the first field:
  - Expected: € ,Deux + recordSeparator
  - Actual: "€",Deux + recordSeparator

- Call flow:
  - CSVPrinter.printRecord delegates to CSVFormat.printRecord, which iterates fields and calls CSVFormat.print(value, out, newRecord) with newRecord = true for the first field.
  - CSVFormat.print converts the value to a CharSequence and calls the private print(Object, CharSequence, …, boolean) method.
  - Since a quote character is configured (RFC4180 uses the default quote '"'), the code enters CSVFormat.printAndQuote.

- In CSVFormat.printAndQuote (QuoteMode MINIMAL is used when getQuoteMode() is null):
  - For a non-empty first field, it checks the first character c with:
    if (newRecord && (c < 0x20 || c > 0x21 && c < 0x23 || c > 0x2B && c < 0x2D || c > 0x7E)) { quote = true; }
  - The Euro character (U+20AC) satisfies c > 0x7E, so quote is set to true solely because the first character is non-ASCII.
  - The method then wraps the value in quotes, producing "€" as the first field.

- Why this is a bug:
  - This conservative heuristic forces quoting for any first-field character outside basic ASCII (> 0x7E), which includes Euro and all CJK characters.
  - The behavior differs from Microsoft Excel and contradicts the test’s expectation: Excel does not quote such values, and the test asserts that RFC4180 should not quote a first field starting with Euro.
  - The rest of MINIMAL logic already scans for actual hazards (delimiter, quote, CR/LF, leading/trailing spaces). The extra condition on non-ASCII at the start is unnecessarily strict and causes over-quoting.

- Conclusion:
  - The root cause is the special-case condition in CSVFormat.printAndQuote for MINIMAL quoting that sets quote = true when the first character of the first field is non-ASCII (c > 0x7E). This leads to quoting "€" and "あ" (CJK) as first fields, failing the test and matching the reported Excel incompatibility.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
CSVFormat.printAndQuote(java.lang.Object, java.lang.CharSequence, int, int, java.lang.Appendable, boolean)
